auditedPrs.notes: Squash commit 719aa88 on main. The PR cites no upstream Go. Its counterpart is the netstack link endpoint in wgengine/netstack, read at the pinned commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55. The PR adds a 4096-packet, 4096*MTU-byte inbound ring in front of the smoltcp netstack. It drops what does not fit, and the egress side stays unbounded. Upstream does the reverse on both sides. Inbound packets go straight into gVisor on the caller's goroutine, with no queue and no queue-full drop. Outbound packets go into a queue of 512 per outbound queue, and a writer blocks there when it is full. The bounding code itself looks correct: the byte budget is released on every refusal path, and buffered_rx is never filled, so no budget leaks. The new tests call the production pump_ingress and WakingPipe::ingress_bounded. Both directions differ from upstream, which gives two findings. A third records that the one inbound ring is shared by every peer and flow on a netstack, so overload from one sender sheds the others' packets too. All three are minor. Neither changes what a peer sees on the wire: TCP recovers dropped segments and UDP is lossy by contract.

gate.detail: Scoped gate on the tree this record ships in: main 3951752 merged into the audit branch, which differs from main only in this file. Run with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 and RUST_TEST_THREADS=4. Every stage exited 0: cargo fmt --all -- --check under the pinned 1.95.0 toolchain; cargo run -p checks; cargo clippy --workspace --exclude ts_cli_util --lib --no-deps --all-features -- -D warnings; the same clippy over bins/tests/benches/examples with -D warnings -A missing_docs; cargo nextest run -p checks -p geiserx_ts_control -p geiserx_ts_runtime -p geiserx_ts_netstack_smoltcp --all-features --no-fail-fast, 1073 run and 1073 green in 39s, with 3 skipped; cargo build --workspace --exclude ts_cli_util --all-targets --all-features. The 3 skipped tests were filtered out on purpose because they need sockets this sandbox blocks: serve_path_proxy_replays_consumed_head_to_backend and proxy_with_prefix_writes_prefix_before_bidi_copy hang on a dropped loopback SYN, and probe_stun_servers_once_sends_binding_request needs outbound UDP. Not run: the full bin/check, because cargo deny is red on any branch (aws-lc bans) and ts_cli_util's tracy feature does not compile under --all-features on this host. Also not run: cargo doc, cargo machete, the doctests, and the test suites of the other workspace crates.

findings.title: Netstack ingress drops on a full ring where upstream delivers inbound packets synchronously, with no queue
findings.detail: Upstream: tstun.Wrapper calls the netstack's PostFilterPacketInboundFromWireGuard hook (netstack.go line 444). That hook, Impl.injectInbound (line 1433), passes an accepted packet to linkEndpoint.gro / injectInbound (netstack.go line 947; link_endpoint.go lines 238-251). That calls the gVisor dispatcher's DeliverNetworkPacket directly on the WireGuard receive goroutine. No ingress queue exists, so a packet that passed the filter is never dropped for lack of queue room. Load is limited by backpressure on the inbound path, and only gVisor's own per-endpoint limits can shed it. Merged: pump_ingress (ts_runtime/src/netstack_actor.rs) puts packets into a 4096-packet, 4096*MTU-byte flume ring with try_send. It drops any packet that does not fit, after the packet was decrypted and passed the filter. The drop is logged only at debug level, and the drop count pump_ingress returns is thrown away by both production callers (netstack_actor.rs and forwarder_actor.rs). So no metric records it. Upstream's own inbound drops are counted in tstun's inboundDroppedPacketsTotal user metric (net/tstun/wrap.go line 247). The PR's reason for dropping instead of waiting is real: the dataplane queue upstream of the pump is an unbounded mpsc: OverlayFromDataplane is mpsc::UnboundedReceiver (ts_runtime/src/dataplane.rs line 147). That is a structural difference from upstream, though, not a port of it. Fixing it means either bounding the dataplane queue so backpressure can reach the underlay, the way Go's synchronous delivery does, or recording this as an intentional fork divergence and exposing the drop count as a metric.

findings.title: Netstack egress stays unbounded where upstream caps each outbound queue at 512 packets with backpressure
findings.detail: Upstream: newLinkEndpoint(512, ...) (netstack.go line 413) gives each outbound queue a 512-slot channel (link_endpoint.go lines 144-163). queue.Write (lines 64-77) blocks the gVisor writer until a slot frees or the queue closes. WritePackets (lines 358-385) stops a batch early on ErrNoBufferSpace. So upstream's stack-to-WireGuard queue is bounded in memory, and the stack is held back while it is full. Merged: WakingPipe::ingress_bounded keeps the device-to-caller direction on flume::unbounded, and the new test egress_is_not_bounded makes that a guarantee. The doc comment says smoltcp's TxToken::consume cannot wait, so a bounded egress would stall the poll loop. smoltcp has a non-blocking way to push back, though: Device::transmit returns Option<TxToken>, and a None makes the interface defer emission to a later poll. WakingPipeDev::transmit (ts_netstack_smoltcp/src/pipe.rs) returns None only when the receiver has disconnected, never when the queue is deep. Replies a peer can provoke, such as RSTs, ICMP and ACKs, plus local application sends, can therefore pile up without limit when the dataplane drains slower than smoltcp emits. That is the same memory-growth class this PR set out to close on ingress, and upstream bounds it. Porting it means bounding the egress channel and having transmit() return None while it is full, the smoltcp form of upstream's blocking queue.Write.

findings.title: One inbound ring is shared by every peer and flow on a netstack, where upstream sheds per endpoint inside the stack
findings.detail: Upstream: with no link-layer inbound queue (linkEndpoint.injectInbound, link_endpoint.go lines 238-251, calls DeliverNetworkPacket on the caller's goroutine), the only place inbound load can be shed is inside gVisor, where each transport endpoint has its own receive buffer. A flow that overruns its endpoint loses its own packets. Merged: each netstack has exactly one ring. pump_ingress (ts_runtime/src/netstack_actor.rs lines 76-112) try_sends every packet the dataplane routed to that netstack into it, whatever peer or flow it belongs to, and drops by arrival order when it is full. The forwarder netstack uses the same pump (ts_runtime/src/forwarder_actor.rs line 154), and it carries every peer's exit and subnet flows. So one authenticated peer that keeps the ring full makes the node drop other peers' packets on that netstack as well. Before #587 that peer could exhaust the host's memory, which is worse, so the bound is still the right trade. But the fate-sharing is new behaviour that upstream does not have, and the PR does not mention it. Closing it means shedding per peer or per flow (a per-source share of the ring, or fair queueing ahead of it) instead of one drop-tail queue.
